page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-8-lssd is an Arm-based cloud virtual machine instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs on the arm64 architecture, 64 GB of system memory, and 805 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage across 2 drives. The instance does not feature dedicated graphics processing units and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio delivers 8 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing this configuration in a memory-dense footprint suitable for memory-sensitive environments. Integrated direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage provides low-latency, high-throughput scratch space, removing network transit overhead for disk operations. Workloads must account for the ephemeral nature of local SSD volumes, necessitating external redundancy or snapshot mechanisms for persistent data.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the utilization of Arm-based dedicated cores combined with high memory density and integrated high-speed local storage offers strong resource consolidation. It eliminates the need to attach supplementary provisioned network disks for transient, high-IOPS operations, optimizing total resource utilization for read-intensive or caching systems.

This server type is suitable for in-memory databases, caching tiers, high-throughput analytics pipelines, and distributed data processing tasks requiring substantial working memory coupled with fast ephemeral NVMe performance.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-8-lssd is an arm64 virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs, 64 GB of memory, and 805 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Characterized by an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, it combines memory density with direct-attached NVMe disks, eliminating the latency and overhead typical of network-attached block storage. The configuration includes no discrete GPU hardware and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By coupling efficient dedicated Arm architecture with fast local storage, the instance delivers a balanced hardware profile for systems requiring extensive memory and immediate I/O throughput. It is well suited for hosting in-memory data stores, distributed caching engines, high-performance database replicas, and data transformation jobs that require rapid scratch disks alongside large in-memory working sets.
